digest.component_or_area: Pandoc corpus verification and testing infrastructure
propositions: Gerrit Verify currently executes complete live-Pandoc corpus processing for every change, consuming significant wall time (184+ seconds on macOS); this work should be replaced with deterministic committed artifacts while preserving all corpus assertions.

The implementation must generate and commit static Pandoc output artifacts covering all corpus inputs and settling passes, organize them by stratum below file-size limits, and validate Pandoc 3.6.1 contract and platform binary SHA-256 values.

Gerrit Verify must drive production segmentation through a fail-closed static converter backed by committed artifacts for all corpus cardinality and safety assertions, while retaining exactly three evidence-selected real product-path bodies (one each from code_arrow, table, and prose strata).

A new external CI job in external-integration.yml must run full corpus replay through installed real Pandoc on a weekly and manual schedule across ubuntu-latest and macos-latest matrix arms, executing every corpus unit and settling pass.

The implementation achieved 90.8% wall-time reduction (42s to 4s baseline) in paired focused testing while preserving all corpus assertions, version probe, platform fingerprint probe, and test matrix coverage across Python and operating-system cells.
